picks.editorial_note: Texas A&M's entry into DOE's Genesis Mission exemplifies a sweeping national push uniting government, industry, and academia around AI, supercomputing, and quantum systems to accelerate scientific discovery — the week's dominant storyline across dozens of institutions.
picks.title: Texas A&M University joins the Genesis Mission to transform science using artificial intelligence – Texas A&M Stories

picks.editorial_note: An $874 million federal commitment to seven companies under the CHIPS and Science Act directly targets the semiconductor supply chain underpinning AI compute — a policy-driven investment with outsized downstream impact on AI research capacity nationwide.
picks.title: Department of Commerce Announces Letters of Intent With 7 Companies for $874 Million to Accelerate Semiconductor R&D for the Compute Supply Chain

picks.editorial_note: Fermilab's deployment of the first AI-driven telescope marks a genuine scientific first, demonstrating how autonomous AI systems can independently direct physical scientific instruments rather than just analyze their data.
picks.title: First AI-driven telescope goes stargazing

picks.editorial_note: UC Davis's brain-computer interface restoring an ALS patient's own voice is a landmark real-world application of AI, showing tangible clinical impact for people with severe neurological disease.
picks.title: Giving People Their Voice

picks.editorial_note: A new $21.5 million NSF AI Institute spanning Penn, Delaware, Delaware State, and Princeton signals sustained federal investment in human-AI collaboration for healthcare, backing a multi-university research infrastructure that will operate for years.
picks.title: Penn partners in new National Science Foundation AI Institute for Human-AI Cooperation | Penn Today

picks.editorial_note: RPI's selection for two Genesis Mission projects, including AI-guided rare-earth element discovery with a national lab, shows how the initiative is already generating concrete, high-value research applications beyond the announcement stage.

picks.editorial_note: Cambridge joining CuspAI's global AI Materials Foundry links UK academic research to an international industry-driven network for AI-accelerated materials discovery, extending the AI-for-science trend beyond U.S. borders.
picks.title: Cambridge researchers contribute to AI Materials Foundry

picks.editorial_note: HKU's ClairS algorithm achieves high-accuracy cancer mutation detection from long-read sequencing across multiple cancer types, a meaningful advance for AI-driven precision oncology diagnostics.
picks.title: HKU School of Computing and Data Science research team develops ClairS, achieving high-accuracy cancer mutation detection across multiple cancer types - All News - Media - HKU

picks.editorial_note: Nebraska's $18 million NSF MRSEC award to study AI-enabled ultra-thin quantum materials represents a major, long-horizon federal investment in the materials science underlying next-generation computing hardware.
picks.title: Husker team earns elite NSF award to drive next generation of materials research

picks.editorial_note: William & Mary's Genesis Mission award to build AI foundation models for particle physics, in partnership with Jefferson Lab and Brookhaven, illustrates how the initiative is fostering deep academic-national lab collaboration in fundamental science.
